chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Muawiya ibn Maysara, that Sinan asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about the man who extends one of his legs in front of him in the prayer while he is seated. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' And I do not see except that he (peace be upon him) said (this) regarding the disabled and the sick. And in another Hadith, 'He prays in a squared position and with both legs extended. All of that is permissible (wide/leeway).'

key_terms.الْمُعْتَلِّ: The disabled / One with a chronic condition

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to extend one's legs while sitting during prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that extending one leg while seated in prayer is not only permissible but characteristic of the sick and elderly, reflecting the principle of ease (yusr) in worship. This narration, found in al-Kafi, underscores the flexibility in prayer postures for those with physical limitations, aligning with the Shia juristic view that the form of prayer adapts to the individual's capacity without invalidating the act of worship. It further confirms the validity of the 'mutarabb'an' posture (sitting with knees spread and one leg extended), demonstrating the breadth of accepted sunnah practices for the infirm.
